answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with an earned-trust ladder: a new identity starts on a barren island with zero earning power and must climb, task by task, like crossing a mesa one knoll at a time. Each step needs completed work attested by a quorum of established peers, and credit decays when idle. A farm minting a thousand clones must climb a thousand ladders of real verified work, so forgery costs as much as honest participation.
